claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **names and ages of the children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather a bit more information about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and living costs?** (For example, is Alex living with you and are you providing for their day-to-day needs?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me. They live with their other parent. But I do help out with some things - I contribute towards clothes and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex lives with their other parent, I need to ask: **Does the other parent currently claim Child Benefit for Alex, or are they not claiming it?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the other parent isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Now, a few more questions to complete the picture:

**What is your nationality or immigration status in the UK?** (For example, are you a British citizen, EU citizen, or do you have settled status or another visa?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, born and raised here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for letting me know that.

**Do you live in the UK?** (And if so, are you normally resident there?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming that.

One more important question:

**Are you the only person who could potentially claim Child Benefit for Alex, or could the other parent (who Alex lives with) also potentially claim?** In other words, would you both be eligible claimants, or is your situation unique in some way?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, the other parent could potentially claim it as well since Alex lives with them. I just know they haven't applied for it yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex's care and upbringing?** Or would you say the other parent (who Alex lives with) has primary responsibility?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd say the other parent has primary responsibility since Alex lives with them full-time. I see Alex regularly, but day-to-day they're with their other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Based on what you've told me, let me explain the situation:

Child Benefit is payable to the person who is responsible for the child. In your case, while you do contribute to Alex's upbringing (such as clothes), Alex lives full-time with the other parent, who has primary responsibility for their day-to-day care and living costs.

The key eligibility requirement is that you must be responsible for the child. Since the other parent has primary responsibility and Alex lives with them full-time, you would not be the qualifying person for Child Benefit purposes, even though you do provide some financial support.

The other parent would be the person eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, as they are the person with primary responsibility for the child's care and living costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I hope this has helped clarify your position. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask.
